title: EXP-082 - Hello World Part 5 Section 5: Rebuild the FX_Orders Form with the Classic Multi-View Wizard (Replacement)
objective: Follow hello-world-pt5.md Section 5 steps 1-7 (06:32-08:15), adapted to FX_ names and the EXP-072 route. In the Web Designer (User scope), record the current User-scoped Form FX_Orders (EXP-072: four business fields), then run New > Classic > Multi-View once with Form Name FX_Orders and Data Source FX_Orders, include the joined and derived properties, order the fields FX_OrderNumber, FX_CustomerID, FX_CusName, FX_CusAddress, FX_Item, FX_ItmsDescription, FX_ItmsCost, FX_Count, FX_DerOrderTotal, FX_ItmsPicture, and accept the explicit replacement prompts for FX_Orders (operator decision 2026-10-14: replace the factory-owned FX_Orders Form). Finish once, perform at most one Designer Save if the Form is dirty, close and reopen it once and verify the components and their bindings. If the wizard does not offer the new properties, a conditional Web Client plus Designer Unload All Global Form Objects pair is authorized once (operator decision 2026-10-14). Captions with missing strings and the runtime check are EXP-083. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt5.md Section 5 (06:32-08:15) with its replacement caution, the EXP-072 record (Classic Multi-View route: New > Category Classic > Wizard MultiView > Form Wizard OK; page 1 Name and Data Source; page 2 Primary Collection; page 3 order with the move-up and move-down arrows and Include checkboxes; final page Save Template unchecked; Finish; Designer Select Form cache and the Form menu recent-forms route), the EXP-076 record (the unload pair and its preference gate), and the EXP-081, EXP-080-R3, EXP-079 and EXP-078 records (the 17 FX_Orders properties and their labels) before browser interaction.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-082-hello-world-part-5-section-5-rebuild-fx-orders-form.md and evidence/EXP-082/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If it expires, follow the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure once and end the task; never sign in inside the portal's embedded app frame (refused, EXP-080-R2) but use the procedure's top-level portal navigation. The Web Designer tab may also have expired; if it shows an expiry or sign-in, record it and stop the task for the coordinator. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection.

Preflight and baseline: the Designer is in User scope and clean. Open the existing FX_Orders Designer Form once (Form menu recent-forms entry or Select Form) and record its Name, ScopeType, ScopeName and the Details > Components list with bindings and captions (expected the EXP-072 eight components); close it again while clean. In the Web Client close the FX_Orders runtime Form if it is open and clean.

Wizard: Web Designer toolbar New > Category Classic > Wizard MultiView > OK (EXP-072 route). Page 1: Name FX_Orders by one plain fill, Form Type MultiView, Data Source FX_Orders; record any message. Page 2: record every property offered and included; include the six new properties FX_CusName, FX_CusAddress, FX_ItmsDescription, FX_ItmsCost, FX_DerOrderTotal, FX_ItmsPicture with the four business fields and leave the system properties as the wizard defaults them, recording each change. Page 3: set the order FX_OrderNumber, FX_CustomerID, FX_CusName, FX_CusAddress, FX_Item, FX_ItmsDescription, FX_ItmsCost, FX_Count, FX_DerOrderTotal, FX_ItmsPicture with single move-up/move-down presses, all Include checked. Final page: Save Template unchecked; record the sentence; Finish once.

Replacement prompts: answer Yes once to each prompt that explicitly asks to replace or overwrite the existing Form FX_Orders (the tutorial shows up to two); record each exact text with a screenshot before answering. Any other prompt, or a replacement prompt naming another Form, means stop without answering Yes.

Conditional unload (only if page 2 does not offer all six new properties): record the missing ones, Cancel the wizard once (nothing is created before Finish); follow EXP-076: read the Web Client User Preference Unload IDO Metadata With Forms read-only (require it checked; Close Window); invoke the Web Client Form > Definition > Unload All Global Form Objects exactly once; with no Form open in the Designer invoke the Designer Form > Definition > Unload All Global Form Objects exactly once; then open the wizard once more and repeat the property check. If a property is still missing, stop blocked without another unload.

After Finish record the response; verify in Details > Components the Form FX_Orders in User scope with one bound component per included property in the set order (bindings object.<Property>), the control types (expected ComboBox for FX_CustomerID and FX_Item, an image-type control for FX_ItmsPicture if the wizard creates one) and each caption as shown (resolved text or raw string ID). Do not edit captions, create strings or change components.
Perform at most one ordinary Designer Save only if the Form is dirty; record the native response and the clean state.

Close the clean FX_Orders Designer Form once through its Form-tab control and reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry (EXP-072); verify Name, ScopeType User, the components, bindings and captions against the post-Finish record.

Capture screenshots of the baseline Form, each wizard page before Next, the final page before Finish, every replacement prompt, the Finish result, the components list, the Save (if any) and the reopened Form; and, if the unload branch runs, the preference reading and both unload menu labels.
Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Classify findings as observed only.
out_of_scope: Creating strings or editing captions (EXP-083); the runtime check (EXP-083); removing component right-click menus and the Section 4 property-class extensions.
Any Form other than FX_Orders; the FX_Orders IDO, its properties and tables; property classes; SQL; runtime records.
Check Out, Check In, Undo Check Out or other checkout-management actions; FormSync, deployment or regeneration; any unload outside the conditional branch.
Direct SQL or script execution, browser JavaScript, console or network inspection, direct URL navigation (except the portal step of the session-expiry procedure), refresh or restart.
Modifying earlier experiment records, AGENTS.md, tutorial sources, recipes or files outside the EXP-082 paths.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Never replace or change any Form other than FX_Orders, and never answer Yes to a prompt that does not explicitly concern replacing FX_Orders.
Never invoke Finish more than once per wizard opening, open the wizard more than twice (the second only after the conditional unload), or retry an ambiguous Finish.

Never invoke an unload unless page 2 lacks one of the six new properties; then exactly one Web Client and exactly one Designer Unload All Global Form Objects, never repeated; never change the Unload IDO Metadata With Forms preference.
Never create or edit a string or caption, never change a component after Finish, and never click the Designer top-toolbar Delete button (Delete Form Definition).
Never invoke the Designer Save more than once or retry an uncertain Save.
Never close a dirty Form or discard changes without operator approval; the wizard Cancel in the conditional branch is approved.
Never change the FX_Orders IDO, its properties, a property class, SQL objects or runtime records.
Never perform check-in, undo checkout or other checkout-management actions, FormSync or deployment.

Never use direct SQL, scripts, application internals or browser JavaScript; never refresh, restart or replace the browser session; re-login only through the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure, at most once per task.
Never claim database durability or replay verification from same-session UI recovery.

artifacts: FX_Orders (User-scoped Designer Form, replaced by the Multi-View wizard)

acceptance_checks.description: Sources reviewed; session usable; Designer in User scope and clean; the existing FX_Orders Form and its components recorded before the wizard. Evidence: baseline screenshots.

One Multi-View wizard (plus one more only after the conditional unload): page 1 Name FX_Orders and Data Source FX_Orders; page 2 includes the six new properties; page 3 order FX_OrderNumber, FX_CustomerID, FX_CusName, FX_CusAddress, FX_Item, FX_ItmsDescription, FX_ItmsCost, FX_Count, FX_DerOrderTotal, FX_ItmsPicture; Save Template unchecked. Evidence: page screenshots and the final page before Finish.

One Finish; each replacement prompt for FX_Orders recorded and answered Yes once; the Finish response recorded. If the unload branch ran: the preference reading and exactly one Web Client and one Designer unload. Evidence: prompt and result screenshots.

The new FX_Orders Form in User scope with one bound component per included property in the set order, control types and captions recorded; at most one Designer Save if dirty. Evidence: components screenshots.
The clean Form closed once and reopened once through the Form menu recent-forms entry; Name, scope, components, bindings and captions recovered. Evidence: reopen screenshots.

The final EXP-082 report gives decisive evidence for AC-1 to AC-5, the complete action audit with exact counts (wizard openings, Finish 1, replacement Yes answers, unloads 0 or exactly 1+1, Save 0 or 1, close/reopen 1, zero strings, zero caption edits, zero IDO changes, zero checkout actions, re-login count), the baseline and new component lists, the worker-written-file inventory and the final state. Repository confinement is supported by worker/harness inventories, with operator git review authoritative. Findings are observed only.
